### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A01, A03, A04 and A05 each appeared in about 49 of 100 traces and A02, A06, A07 and A08 in about 52 of 100; in the later window the first group appears in about 55 of 100 traces and the second in about 46 of 100, with no repeats of these activities within traces in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008]
- In the loop over A03, A04 and A05, the earlier window showed both directions of every pair at nearly equal shares (A03→A04 about 34% versus A04→A03 about 32%, A03→A05 about 32% versus A05→A03 about 34%, A04→A05 about 35% versus A05→A04 about 33%), i.e. no fixed order; in the later window one direction dominates each pair (A03→A05 about 43%, A05→A04 about 41%, A04→A03 about 44%) while the reverse directions fall to about 21–27%. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- The order of A06 and A07 flipped: earlier the dominant steps ran A08→A06 (about 42% of A08's outgoing transitions) and then A06→A07 (about 40%); in the later window they run A08→A07 (about 42%) and A07→A06 (about 40%), with A08→A06 down to about 25% and A07→A09 down from about 42% to 31%. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- Around A23 and A24 the internal order of two pairs also reversed: earlier, A28 sent about 58% of its outgoing transitions to A27 and A27 about 58% on to A24, while A30 sent about 58% to A29 and A29 about 58% to A24; later, A27 sends about 54% to A28 and A28 about 54% to A24, and A29 sends about 49% to A30 with A30 sending about 49% to A24. A23 itself routed about 20% of its outgoing transitions to A27 earlier versus about 30% later, and about 30% to A30 earlier versus about 23% later; participation rose for A27 and A28 (about 48% to 55% of traces) and fell for A29 and A30 (about 53% to 46%). [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, DIR015, DIR016, DIR017, DIR018, DIR019]
- Smaller shifts of the same kind appear elsewhere: from A17, the share continuing to A23 fell from about 60% to about 47% in favour of A18 and A19, with A16's participation up from about 49% to 53% of traces and A17's down from about 52% to 48% [OCC015, OCC016, DIR010, DIR011, DIR013]; from A36, the share returning to A35 rose from about 34% to about 46% at the expense of A39 (about 66% to 54%), and A33 and A37/A38 occur somewhat more often per trace or in more traces (A33 from about 0.78 to 0.88 occurrences per trace at roughly unchanged participation) [DIR022, DIR023, DIR024, OCC024, OCC027, OCC028].
- Every activity and successor pair named above is observed in both windows and no participation falls to zero, so all of these differences are shifts in how often existing behaviour occurs rather than activities or paths appearing or disappearing. [OCC001, OCC019, DIR003, DIR015, DIR023]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Every difference is a moderate shift in the shares of activities and edges that are well observed in both windows, spread across several unrelated regions (A01–A09, A16–A23, A27–A30, A33–A39), and even the largest differences are exceeded by a few percent of the random reference splits; without an expected-count baseline for the screening, this scattered pattern cannot be distinguished from sampling variation between two 200-trace samples [OCC001, DIR003, DIR016, DIR023].
